subject: Genetics
title: Polygenic Risk Scores
description: A 60-second lesson on Polygenic Risk Scores.

hook.text: Heart disease isn't one gene. Thousands of tiny variants add up. A polygenic risk score sums them all.

buildup.text: GWAS finds variants linked to disease. Each nudges risk slightly. Together they form a meaningful prediction.

discovery.text: People in the top 5% for heart disease PRS face triple the risk of those in the bottom 5%.

twist.text: PRS works best for Europeans because most studies used European data. Other groups get less accurate scores.

climax.text: Polygenic scores could enable early prevention—if they work equally well for every population. Equity matters.

punchline.text: Thousands of tiny risks. One score. Early warning.

quiz.question: What does a polygenic risk score measure?
options: The combined effect of many variants on disease risk
